questions.text: The potential of the field at point E is -8 V. Find the potential energy (mJ) acquired by a particle with a charge of 5 mC brought to this point from infinity.
When a charge of 4 $\mu$C is moved from point A to point B in a uniform electrostatic field (as in the figure), 96 $\mu$J of work is done. What is the magnitude of the field strength (V/m)?
How much work (in joules) is done in moving a positive charge of $2 \cdot 10^{-7}$ C from a point of an electrostatic field with a potential of 40 V to a point with a potential of –10 V?
How much work (in joules) does the electric field do in moving a positive charge of 1 C from point 1 to point 2? The potential difference between the points is 10 V.
Moving a charge of $1.2 \cdot 10^{-4}$ C from one point to another required 0.6 mJ of work. Determine the potential difference between the points (V).

As a result of moving an electron from one point to another in an electric field, its kinetic energy changed by $8 \cdot 10^{-19}$ J. What is the potential difference between these two points (V)? $e=1.6 \cdot 10^{-19}$ C.

The speed of an electron in an electric field increased from $1 \cdot 10^7$ to $5 \cdot 10^7$ m/s. What is the potential difference between the initial and final points (kV)? The charge-to-mass ratio of the electron is $1.76 \cdot 10^{11}$ C/kg.
If the potential difference between points 2 and 3 in the uniform electric field shown in the diagram is 6 V, what work ($\mu$J) is done in moving a charge of 3.5 $\mu$C between points 1 and 3?

Points 1, 2 and 3 in the uniform electric field shown in the diagram correspond to the vertices of an equilateral triangle. If the potential difference between points 1 and 3 is 16 V, what work ($\mu$J) is done in moving a charge of 2.5 $\mu$C between points 2 and 3?
What is the relationship between the field strengths and potentials at different points (1, 2, 3, 4) of the electric field of two charged planes (a parallel-plate capacitor)?
Which of the following relations is correct for the works done in moving a positive point charge in a uniform electrostatic field from point O to points 1, 2, 3, 4 in turn?
How does the potential of a point charge change when the distance from the charge to the point under consideration increases by a factor of 4?
The field strength of a point charge at a point 3.5 cm from the charge is 150 V/m and is directed toward the charge. What is the potential of the field at that point (V)?

Point charges $+q$ and $+2q$ are located at a distance of $2r$ from each other. The potential at point A, located midway between them, is 3 V. When, at a distance of $2r$ from point A, a point charge $Q$ was placed, the potential at that point became -3 V. Find the charge $Q$.
Charges $+2q$ and $-q$ are placed as shown in the figure. What is the potential difference between points M and N?
Charges $+3q$ and $+4q$ are placed as shown in the figure. What is the potential difference between points M and N?
If the resultant electric field strength of the four charges in the figure at point O is 25 V/m, what is the resultant potential at that point (in volts)?
The surface charge density is the same on metal spheres of radii $R_1=R$ and $R_2=2R$. Compare the potentials at the centers of the spheres.
What are the field strength and the potential at the center of a charged conducting sphere of radius 10 cm and potential 200 V?
Spheres x and y, whose potentials and radii are shown in the figure, were brought into contact. What will the potential of the spheres be afterward?
Sphere K in the figure was touched first to sphere L and then to sphere M. What will the charges of the spheres be afterward?
